nodes.purpose: Finding + Review pydantic models. Depends on nothing.
Parse unified diff into changed files/hunks/line ranges.
Shared specialist shape: prompt, LLM call, parse, error handling.
Merge 4 Finding lists, dedupe by file+line, compute overall_confidence, apply HITL gate.
Fan out to specialists in parallel, collect partials, hand to aggregator.
Append-only events spine: one time-ordered row per action.
LLM client wrapper: timeout, retry, structured output.
Read PR diff. Read-only scope in this milestone set.

INV-1-dependency-direction.rule: Dependencies point inward only: entry -> app -> domain -> core. core/ (contracts.py, diff.py) imports nothing from this package; agents/ never import orchestrator, cli, github, or events.
INV-1-dependency-direction.why: Study ADR-002 dependency rule. Keeps the specialists testable offline with zero network and zero I/O, which is what makes M1's demo command runnable in CI.
INV-1-dependency-direction.check: python -c "import ast,pathlib,sys; bad=[(p,n.module) for p in pathlib.Path('src/prreview').rglob('*.py') for n in ast.walk(ast.parse(p.read_text())) if isinstance(n,ast.ImportFrom) and n.module and ((p.name in ('contracts.py','diff.py') and 'prreview' in n.module) or ('agents/' in str(p) and any(m in n.module for m in ('orchestrator','cli','github','events'))))]; print(bad); sys.exit(1 if bad else 0)"
INV-1-dependency-direction.violation_means: A specialist has grown a hidden dependency on the outside world. Tests will start needing network.

INV-2-every-outbound-call-has-a-timeout.rule: Every network call (LLM, GitHub API) is made through llm.py or github.py and passes an explicit timeout. No bare requests/httpx/anthropic call anywhere else in the tree.
INV-2-every-outbound-call-has-a-timeout.why: Study §0.2 'Tool / API timeout' failure mode + §4.1 Phase 12. A CI job that hangs forever is the prototype's most likely real-world failure, and it is invisible until it happens.
INV-2-every-outbound-call-has-a-timeout.check: ! grep -rnE '(httpx|requests)\.(get|post)\(|anthropic\.[A-Z]|Anthropic\(' src/prreview --include='*.py' | grep -vE 'src/prreview/(llm|github)\.py' ; for f in src/prreview/llm.py src/prreview/github.py; do [ -f "$f" ] && { grep -q 'timeout' "$f" || { echo "no timeout in $f"; exit 1; }; }; done; echo 'INV-2 ok'
INV-2-every-outbound-call-has-a-timeout.check_note: The github.py half is conditional: that file does not exist until M5, and an invariant whose own command errors on a missing future file reports failure regardless of code state.
INV-2-every-outbound-call-has-a-timeout.violation_means: An unbounded wait exists. The system can now fail fast-but-hung instead of slower-but-correct.

INV-3-no-ungrounded-finding.rule: Every Finding's file_path must appear in the parsed diff, and line_start/line_end must fall inside a hunk range of that file. Findings failing this are dropped and counted, never shown.
INV-3-no-ungrounded-finding.why: Study §0.2 'Hallucination in a critical path' and the stated quality bar. A finding pointing at a nonexistent line is the single most credibility-destroying output this tool can produce.
INV-3-no-ungrounded-finding.violation_means: The reviewer is hallucinating locations. Trust in every other finding drops to zero.

INV-4-no-unattended-write.rule: No code path posts to GitHub without an explicit human approval step. The GitHub token used in this milestone set is read-only.
INV-4-no-unattended-write.why: The autonomy level chosen at G0 is 'Human reviews output' (study §0.3 level 2). Enforced at the credential layer as well as in code so a bug cannot escalate autonomy.
INV-4-no-unattended-write.violation_means: The agent can speak in your name. This is the one failure the HITL design exists to prevent.
